entertainment.title: ‘Nobody Wants This’ Season 3 Review: Kristen Bell and Adam Brody’s Netflix Romance Levels Up but Can’t Ditch Old Habits
entertainment.summary: Justine Lupe, Timothy Simons and Jackie Tohn also return, as the central couple — a rabbi and a former agnostic preparing to convert to Judaism — take a big step forward in their relationship.
entertainment.body:
If nothing else, give Nobody Wants This credit for allowing itself a tiny bit of growth: After two seasons of exhaustingly circular conflict about whether a good-boy rabbi like Noah ( Adam Brody ) could ever really be with an agnostic Gentile sex podcaster like Joanne ( Kristen Bell ), season three begins not only with the couple moving in together, but Joanne starting Jewish conversion classes.

Finally, we’ve graduated from asking if to asking how . For a show whose very dithering had previously seemed to reflect Joanne’s fear that “no one wants to listen to happy,” it’s a welcome step forward. But as lifelong flake Joanne has learned many times over by now, wherever you go, there you are. Nobody Wants This might be on its way to becoming a sweeter, more even-keeled version of itself, but it can’t completely shake the bad habits that have made it nearly as exasperating as it is endearing. Related Stories Movies BlumFest Haunts New York Comic Con 2026: All the Highlights From Blumhouse Atomic Monster TV 'Nobody Wants This' Consulting Rabbi Slams Star Adam Brody's Gaza "Genocide" Comments Nobody Wants This The Bottom Line As endearing and exasperating as ever. Airdate: Thursday, Oct. 22 (Netflix) Cast: Adam Brody, Kristen Bell, Justine Lupe, Timothy Simons, Jackie Tohn, Tovah Feldshuh, Paul Ben-Victor, Stephanie Faracy, Michael Hitchcock Creator: Erin Foster

Admittedly, it does feel good to bask for once in what feels right about Joanne and Noah’s relationship rather than fret over what might be wrong about it. The lovebirds are so giddy they wake each other up in the middle of the night just to coo: “Hey. We live together.” Nothing can pierce their romantic bliss, not even minor annoyances like Joanne’s inability to ever shut a cabinet door (“It’s like living with a ghost,” Noah complains adorably) or bigger ones like her almost sabotaging their first trip as a couple when she runs into a desperately needy fan (creator Erin Foster ) at the airport.

Not, at this point, that there’s anyone or anything trying to ruin them anyway. With Joanne’s no-seriously-this-time decision to convert, previously insurmountable obstacles have melted away. Noah’s old temple is only too relieved to bring him back for a trial run, now that they’ve been reassured his life partner will soon become part of their tribe. His disapproving mother (Tovah Feldshuh) is all too happy to throw herself into turning her possible future daughter-in-law into the perfect rebbetzin (rabbi’s wife). There’s nothing at all standing between them and happily ever after, or so it seems.

entertainment.title: ‘The Great And Unmatched’: John Anderson Remembered by Blake Shelton, Tim McGraw & More
entertainment.summary: The country music community is paying tribute to Anderson, who died Wednesday, Oct. 21 at the age of 71.
entertainment.body:
The late country music great John Anderson has gone, but his music will never die.

That’s the sentiment from the country music community, as Anderson’s fans, friends and collaborators remember the pioneer and hitmaker who passed away Wednesday, Oct. 21, at the age of 71 .

Born December 13, 1954, and raised in Apopka, FL, Anderson relocated to Nashville after he completed high school. It proved to be the right move. In 1976, Anderson signed with Warner Bros. Records, and would turn the pages of a songbook that includes “Swingin’,” “Straight Tequila Night,” “Seminole Wind,” and many others. Explore John Anderson See latest videos, charts and news

A commercial success, he collected 20 top 10s on Billboard ‘s Hot Country Songs chart, including five No. 1s, and nabbed five top 10s on the Top Country Albums tally. In a career spanning almost five decades, Anderson filled his boots with industry plaudits, too, including the Academy of Country Music’s career achievement award in 1993, induction into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2014, and elevation into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024 , a member of a class that included Toby Keith and James Burton. Related Jordan Davis' Latest Radio Single Is a 'Mess': 'The Melody Just Locked Me In' Lily Allen Tells Fans She's 'Gutted' To Miss Auckland Show Due to Viral Infection Emmylou Harris, Elvis Costello, Black Crowes to Pay Tribute to Gram Parsons Ahead of Posthumous Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction

“There is too much for me to say about John Anderson in just a statement. I am sick and I am stunned. But I am a very lucky man,” he writes on social media . “I got the opportunity to find out that my hero wasn’t just the guy I hoped he’d be. He was so much more than that. John was my friend.”

Shelton collaborated with Anderson on the 2020 release “Tuesday I’ll Be Gone.” “I got to see him last Sunday and I don’t even know why but I told him I loved him,” he continues. “That is what fills my heart in this moment. My love and prayers go out to John’s family. This one really hurts.”

John Rich produced Anderson’s 2007 album Easy Money , and admired the artist. “I’ve just learned that my favorite country artist of all time, and a man I called ‘Uncle John’ for the past 20 years has passed away,” the Big & Rich co-founder recounts . “The great and unmatched John Anderson…He loved Jesus, and his family and his country. He was a massive influence on me in more ways that I can count. I love you, Uncle John.”

entertainment.body:
The Chilean artists enter YouTube ’s Billion Views Club with the official music video for “Gata Only.” Released in March 2024, the viral hit is the first for either artist to pass the 1 billion view threshold.

Fueled by its poolside visual and TikTok users, the flowing reggaetón would go on to top several charts and peaked at No. 27 on the Billboard Hot 100, for FloyyMenor’s first appearance on the national singles tally and Cris MJ’s second career entry . Explore Cris Mj FloyyMenor See latest videos, charts and news

Indeed, “Gata Only” was FloyyMenor’s first song to impact any Billboard chart . The breakout singer, songwriter and rapper made it count. By April, “Gata Only” had climbed to No. 1 on the Hot Latin Songs. With that feat, the countrymen became the first Chileans to enter the top 10 on the chart in 25 years, since La Ley and Ednita Nazario’s “Tú Sabes Bien.” It would spend 14 consecutive weeks at the top of the leaderboard, en route to topping Billboard ’s year-end Hot Latin Songs chart . “Super happy with this achievement,” the-then 18-year-old told Billboard at the time. “I’m grateful to the people who have supported me since my beginnings. It was difficult for me to get where I am, but we’ve reached one of the goals I had.”

Internationally, the song became his first top 10 on the Billboard Global Excl. U.S. chart, and logged multiple weeks atop the Chile Songs chart.

He also made history as the first Chilean to illuminate the Empire State Building in the colors of his national flag, doing so in October 2024 during Hispanic Heritage Month.

It was a dream come true for the youngster. “When I was a kid, my dream was always to speak English and come to the United States,” FloyyMenor told Billboard Español in 2024.

entertainment.title: Live Nation Adds North Melbourne Venue to Australian Portfolio
entertainment.summary: The concerts giant will deliver and operate a new purpose-built venue at Arden Central, about one mile from the city’s CBD.
entertainment.body:
MELBOURNE, Australia — Live Nation’s Australian portfolio of live music venues continues to grow with the addition of a new 5,000-capacity space in North Melbourne.

The concerts giant will deliver and operate the purpose-built venue at Arden Central, a major multi-billion-dollar, government-backed urban renewal and innovation precinct, about one mile from the city’s CBD. Related Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania Rachel Scharf

Once completed, the site is expected to host more than 100 events each year, creating “new performance opportunities for Australian artists and local talent, attract international touring acts and give fans another place to experience live music,” reads a statement from LN.

Announced Thursday, Oct. 22, the venue is part of the first stage of Arden Central, a cultural and parkland neighborhood being developed by Hamton and Hostplus and serviced by train.

“Melbourne is one of the world’s great live music cities, and continued investment in venues is essential to attracting international artists and keeping Melbourne relevant in an increasingly competitive global environment,” comments Alex Klos , president, Australia & New Zealand at Live Nation. “This purpose-built venue will add a significant new stage to Melbourne’s live music ecosystem, while helping establish Arden Central as a vibrant new destination for live entertainment.”

The wider precinct, budgeted at A$7 billion, should provide more than 5,400 homes for over 10,000 people, alongside retail, hospitality, community facilities and 5.5 hectares of open space.

There, LN joins new precinct partners Melbourne Victory Football Club and the University of Melbourne, plus the North Melbourne Football Club, the four-time VFL/AFL premiers which has called Arden Street home for more than 125 years.

With a 5,000-capacity, LN’s newest venue is one of its biggest in these parts. Currently, the live entertainment juggernaut operates The Palais Theatre (2,900 capacity) and Festival Hall in Melbourne, Fortitude Music Hall (3,000) and The Triffid (800) in Brisbane, Hindley Street Music Hall in Adelaide (1,800), Anita’s Theatre in Wollongong (1,200), and the Northbridge Music Hall in Perth, which is expected to open to the public in the summer of 2026-27. LN also operates the 13,000-capacity Spark Arena in Auckland, New Zealand.

entertainment.body:
John Anderson , the Country Music Hall of Fame inductee with a distinctive voice and a weighty songbook that included “Swingin’,” “Straight Tequila Night,” and “Seminole Wind,” died today (Oct. 21) at the age of 71. Explore John Anderson See latest videos, charts and news

“It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend,” reads a statement from his family. Related Jordan Davis' Latest Radio Single Is a 'Mess': 'The Melody Just Locked Me In' Lily Allen Tells Fans She's 'Gutted' To Miss Auckland Show Due to Viral Infection Emmylou Harris, Elvis Costello, Black Crowes to Pay Tribute to Gram Parsons Ahead of Posthumous Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction

Anderson, who attended the Country Music Hall of Fame induction ceremony to herald this year’s honorees on Sunday (Oct. 18), died peacefully in his sleep, reads the statement from his family, roughly seven weeks before his 72nd birthday. “His music will live on, but for us, his greatest legacy will always be the love he gave his family and the memories we will carry with us forever. Please keep our family in your thoughts and prayers as we grieve this unimaginable loss.”

“To the world, he was a gifted country music singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives. To us, he was so much more. He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely, and made every ordinary moment feel special. We are completely heartbroken.”

His fellow country artists were remembering him as a singular talent. “There is too much for me to say about John Anderson in just a statement,” posted Blake Shelton on X. “I am sick and I am stunned. But I am a very lucky man. I got the opportunity to find out that my hero wasn’t just the guy I hoped he’d be. He was so much more than that. John was my friend.”

John Rich called Anderson “my favorite country artist of all time…He was a massive influence on me in more ways that I can count. I love you, Uncle John.”

A native of Apopka, Fla., Anderson relocated to Nashville in 1971. An early job saw him nailing shingles onto the roof of the Grand Ole Opry House ahead of that iconic building’s 1974 opening.

“I was just wanting to play and sing pretty much at any level that I could,” he told Billboard in 2024. “Thankfully, I was blessed that one little job led to another one, and most of the time it was kind of a little upgrade.”

David Krumholtz is sharing why he missed the 10 Things I Hate About You reunion during Julia Stiles ‘ tribute to Heath Ledger on Dancing With the Stars Tuesday night.

In a video posted on Instagram Wednesday, the actor explained that he’s currently in the Catskill Mountains in upstate New York filming a movie.

“I could not be in L.A. for Dancing With the Stars last night. I would have loved loved loved to have been there,” he said. “Everyone looked so amazing. Julia’s tribute to my dear friend, who I miss every single day, was amazing and stunning, and I’m so proud of her.” Related Stories TV Val Chmerkovskiy Returns to 'Dancing With the Stars' After One-Episode Suspension Movies Julia Stiles Reunites With '10 Things I Hate About You' Cast to Honor Heath Ledger on 'DWTS'

“I thought the cast looked amazing. They all look so young still,” Krumholtz added before taking off his hat to show his newly bald head. He quipped that “it would have been weird” to join his former co-stars in the ballroom after shaving “what’s left of my hair” because it would have become “internet fodder.”

“I didn’t want that, but that’s not why I wasn’t there. I would have dealt with it. Anyway, love them all, love you all,” he concluded.

During the latest DWTS episode , Stiles and her pro partner Ezra Sosa dedicated their dance to Ledger, who starred opposite Stiles in the beloved 1999 rom-com. He died in 2008 at the age of 28 from an accidental overdose.

The pair danced to “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” by Frankie Valli, which was the song Ledger’s Patrick Verona serenaded Stiles’ Kat Stratford with during her soccer practice at the high school stadium. In the scene, he runs and dances across the stands as the marching band plays to try and win her over after Joey Donner (Andrew Keegan) pays him to take Kat out.

Following Stiles and Sosa’s emotional dance, which featured some of Ledger’s iconic moves, the poem her character reads in the film about Patrick starts playing in the ballroom. After the actress lays a flower on the ground in honor of Ledger, she is joined by her fellow 10 Things I Hate About You co-stars, including Keegan, Joseph Gordon-Levitt (Cameron James), Larisa Oleynik (Bianca Stratford), Gabrielle Union (Chastity) and Susan May Pratt (Mandella).
